sections.body:
This is a story about a boy called An. An is eight years old. He has short black hair and very steady eyes.

An always tells the truth. That is his habit. If somebody asks him how many sweets he has, he counts them properly. If somebody asks him what he did yesterday, he tells them what really happened.

Every good story has three parts. It has a beginning, a middle and an end. The beginning tells you who the story is about. The middle is where something goes wrong. The end is where everything comes right again.

An's story begins on a sunny afternoon with a football and a blue bowl. The middle is the worst minute of his life. The end is a surprise, and it is a good one.

This story is not about being clever. It is about a boy who finds out something about telling the truth that most people learn much later.
examples: This is the beginning of An's story.
The middle is the part where An is afraid.
The end is the part where everybody is happy.
sections.heading: A boy whose words were always true

sections.body:
Mum's blue bowl stood on the shelf in the kitchen. It was old. It had a small chip on the rim, and it was the bowl she used for soup on cold days.

An was playing football in the yard. He was doing kick-ups against the wall. His little sister came out to watch, and she stood right where he was kicking.

He did not mean to hit her. But the ball went too fast. It went past her and hit the kitchen shelf.

There was a sound like a bell.

An went in and looked. Blue pieces were on the floor. The biggest piece was under the table. His mother was at the table with her tea, and she turned round.

"An," she said. "What did you do?"

An's stomach felt cold. He could say "nothing". He could say the wind blew it. He could say nothing at all, and go outside, and it would be over.

But the blue pieces were all over the floor, and his sister was crying in the yard, and An's feet would not move.

"Mum," he said. "That was me. I was kicking the ball and it hit the shelf."
examples: Mum, that was me. I was kicking the ball.
The wind did not break the bowl. I did.
I am sorry, Mum. I broke your blue bowl.
sections.heading: The day An broke the blue bowl

sections.body:
The kitchen went very quiet.

Mum looked at the floor. Then she looked at An. An stood still and did not look away.

"Your grandfather made that bowl," said Mum. "And you told me the truth, and you did not try to hide it."

Then she did something An did not expect. She put her arms around him.

"Thank you," she said. "Do you know how hard that was for you? Thank you for telling me."

An did not understand yet. He thought telling the truth would make the trouble worse. It had made it smaller.

After that, things got better in a quiet way. An swept up the blue pieces with the little brush. He put the biggest piece in his pocket, and he asked Auntie Mai to glue it, and it looked almost perfect again.

And then came the surprise of the day.

At the shop, An saw the old lady from number 9. She was crying. Her dog had run away, and she could not find it. An thought about his own dog, Tico, who was exactly like that at home: silly, slow and always hungry.

An had seen a small brown dog near the school gates that morning. He had told the truth about it then too, because his teacher had asked.

"I think it is by the school gates," he said. "I saw a dog there this morning."

The old lady ran. An ran after her. The little brown dog was there, eating a bun.

"Thank you, little boy," said the old lady. "You are the first one who told me where to look."
examples: Thank you for telling me the truth.
I saw a dog by the school gates this morning.
I did not mean to break it.
sections.heading: What happened after An told the truth

sections.body:
An had never practised this. He just did it. Still, you can borrow his way, step by step, when you have done something wrong.

You can use these steps any time you need to say a hard true thing.
examples: I did it. I am sorry.
I want to tell you something true.
I am not going to blame anybody else.
sections.heading: How An found the words to tell the truth
steps: Stop. Do not run away and do not blame someone else.
Look at what really happened. Say it to yourself first.
Find the person who needs to know.
Say the true thing in one short sentence. Do not hide inside a long one.
Say sorry for the part that was your fault.
Stay there and listen. The answer may be kinder than you feared.

sections.body:
These are the new words in this story. Read them once, then read the story again and find them.

The **truth** is what really happened, even when it is not the easy thing to say.

A **lie** is when you say something you know is not true, on purpose, to make things easier for yourself.

A **promise** is something you say you will do. A promise you do not keep is a broken promise, and people remember it for a long time.

To be **brave** about something means to do the hard part while you are still afraid. Bravery is not the absence of fear.
sections.heading: The words about truth

terms.example: An told his mother the truth about the blue bowl.
terms.gloss: What really happened, even when it is not the easy thing to say.

terms.example: He could have said the wind broke the bowl, but that would be a lie.
terms.gloss: Saying something you know is not true, on purpose, to make things easier for yourself.

terms.example: An promised to tell his mother everything from then on.
terms.gloss: Something you say you will do. People remember a broken promise for a long time.

terms.example: He was brave, and his hands were shaking.
terms.gloss: Doing the hard part while you are still afraid. Bravery is not the absence of fear.

sections.body:
That night, An lay in bed and thought about the day. The broken bowl. His mother's arms. The old lady on the step, holding her dog.

The lesson in this story is small, and it is worth keeping. An expected the truth to make things worse. Instead, it made everything smaller. A worry that is hidden grows bigger every hour. A worry that is said out loud can be carried by two people instead of one.

So the next time you have done something you wish you had not done, you do not have to be perfect. You only have to be quick, before the story turns into a lie of your own.
examples: A worry that is hidden grows bigger every hour.
Tell it quickly, before it becomes a lie.
sections.heading: What An learned

item.summary: An always tells the truth, even when the truth is hard to say. Follow him through the day he breaks his mother's blue bowl. You will learn the three parts of the story, four new words, and what happened when he chose not to hide.
item.title: The Boy Who Always Told the Truth
